notes.front: What are the Scrum values, in one sentence?
notes.back: Five values that successful use of Scrum depends on people living ever more proficiently: commitment, focus, openness, respect and courage.
notes.explanation: They give direction to the team’s work, actions and behaviour. When they are lived, the empirical pillars come to life and build trust.
notes.example: Like a band that agrees to show up, play the same song, say when something is off, trust each other’s skill, and try the hard part.

notes.front: How many Scrum values are there?
notes.explanation: Commitment, focus, openness, respect and courage.

notes.front: The Scrum Team {{c1::commits}} to achieving its goals and to supporting each other.
notes.explanation: This is the value of commitment.

notes.front: The Scrum Team’s primary {{c1::focus}} is on the work of the Sprint, to make the best possible progress toward its goals.
notes.explanation: This is the value of focus.

notes.front: The Scrum Team and its stakeholders are {{c1::open}} about the work and the challenges.
notes.explanation: This is the value of openness.

notes.front: Scrum Team members {{c1::respect}} each other to be capable, independent people.
notes.explanation: This is the value of respect; they are also respected as such by the people they work with.

notes.front: Scrum Team members have the {{c1::courage}} to do the right thing and to work on tough problems.
notes.explanation: This is the value of courage.

notes.front: What effect should how a team practises Scrum have on the Scrum values?
notes.back: It should reinforce them, not diminish or undermine them.
notes.explanation: The Scrum Team learns and explores the values as it works with the events and artifacts.

notes.front: The team shares its real progress and problems with stakeholders instead of reporting that all is well. Which value is this most directly?
notes.back: Openness: being open about the work and the challenges.
notes.choices:
A) Openness
B) Focus
C) Respect
notes.choicesExplained: B: focus is about concentrating on the work of the Sprint. C: respect is about seeing each other as capable, independent people.
notes.explanation: The Scrum Guide ties openness to the work and its challenges, shared with stakeholders.

notes.front: Mid-Sprint, a Developer turns down side projects to keep working on the work of the Sprint. Which value is this most directly?
notes.back: Focus: the primary focus is on the work of the Sprint.
notes.choices:
A) Focus
B) Openness
C) Respect
notes.choicesExplained: B: openness is about being open about the work and challenges. C: respect is about seeing each other as capable, independent people.
notes.explanation: Focus keeps the team making the best possible progress toward its goals.
